purpose: Teach: オペラ/ラップ/スカウト/モバイル/プログラミング/思い切り/新車/停車

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さんと、絶対、オペラ、絶対、見に行ったわよな、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran, do you remember? When we were young, your father and I actually went to see the opera together.
lines.style: Soft opening, almost wistful. Gentle emphasis on 'Gran' as if reaching back through time. Unhurried pace, letting the memory settle in the air. Slight lift at 'opera' — real pride in the memory.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、ラジオで、絶対、ラップ、絶対、初めて、絶対、聞いた時、絶対、驚いたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes. I do. I remember the first time your grandfather played rap on the radio — I was so surprised, dear.
lines.style: Knowing warmth with a thread of gentle teasing underneath. Light, almost playful cadence. A small smile in the voice. She's remembering his surprise more than her own.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、野球で、絶対、スカウト、絶対、声、絶対、かけられたぞ、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When we were young, do you remember? Your father got scouted for baseball. They actually called out to him.
lines.style: Wistful, with a note of quiet pride. Slight pause before 'scouted' — letting the weight of that moment breathe. Warm address to 'Gran.' Trailing off gently, inviting her to complete the memory with him.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、モバイル、絶対、なんて、絶対、知らなかったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Your grandfather had no idea what a mobile phone was back then. Do you remember that, dear?
lines.style: Playful, almost conspiratorial tone. A gentle laugh threaded through. Light and quick — she's enjoying the absurdity of how much has changed. Warm toward him.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、プログラミング、絶対、と、絶対、いう、絶対、言葉、絶対、覚え始めたぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: Do you remember? When we were young, your father started learning programming. That was when the word 'programming' even entered his vocabulary.
lines.style: Slow, measured nostalgia. Slight wonder in the voice — looking back at how much has changed. Gentle emphasis on 'programming' as a word that marks an era. Reaching toward her with the question.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、思い切り、絶対、お仕事、絶対、頑張ったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Your grandfather worked so hard when he was young. Do you remember how much effort he put into everything, dear?
lines.style: Tender, steady warmth. No hurry. Speaking with quiet admiration. Soft beginning, like she's touching a memory carefully. Gentle affection in her voice toward him.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、新車、絶対、買えた時、絶対、誇らしかったぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: Do you remember, Gran? When we were young, your father bought that new car. I remember how proud he was.
lines.style: Wistful, almost marveling. Gentle voice reflecting that long-ago pride. The memory lands softly. Patient pacing, letting each detail settle. Warmth toward 'Gran,' reaching back together.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、駅前、絶対、停車、絶対、して、絶対、ばあさんを、絶対、迎えに来てくれたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: He used to pick me up from the station in front — do you remember that, dear? He'd be waiting there.
lines.style: Very tender, deeply intimate. Quiet voice, as if speaking to something precious. Slow, savoring each detail. Soft exhale at the end — the memory itself is the gift. Genuine gratitude in every word.
